claims.head: A shadow job for DeBrincat, Finnie and Brandsegg-Nygård
claims.call: The Red Wings’ L2 (DeBrincat, Finnie and Brandsegg-Nygård) spends at least 47% of its 5-on-5 time against the Flyers’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Red Wings keep sending DeBrincat’s line (DeBrincat, Finnie and Brandsegg-Nygård) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Todd McLellan has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Flyers’ first line is Couturier, Tippett and Zegras.
claims.nums: At home: 47% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 34% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Todd McLellan likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Flyers’ first line.

claims.head: Where the Red Wings have the edge: shot volume
claims.body: The Red Wings are around the middle of the league for shot volume, and the Flyers are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 8 games cover only 16% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 47%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
David Jiříček has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 41% of the team’s power-play time in 6 games, up from 2% last season.

They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 4 of their last 6 games, including the last one. Viktor Arvidsson takes shifts on two lines, L1 and L4. Axel Sandin-Pellikka is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Faulk and Englund.

DET.head: The Red Wings have a lot going for them
DET.body: Detroit has home-ice advantage and has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Flyers’ way back in is keeping dangerous shots away.

PHI.head: Not an easy night for the Flyers
PHI.body: Detroit has home-ice advantage and has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Flyers can pull it off if they keep dangerous shots away.

story.head: Somebody has to win
paras: The Red Wings are winless in three (0-1-2). The Flyers are winless in eight (0-5-3). Both teams are near the bottom of the standings.
At home, Todd McLellan likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Flyers’ first line. The Red Wings have the edge over the Flyers on shot volume.

items.text: Alex DeBrincat is two goals from 300.
The Flyers have been without Cam York and Travis Konecny for several games.
The Red Wings have been without J.T. Compher since Oct 4, and have had to make do without Simon Edvinsson all season.
Lucas Raymond has a point in five straight games against Philadelphia.
